solutions.latex:
$\sin x=\dfrac{2}{5}$, so the adjacent side is $\sqrt{5^2-2^2}=\sqrt{21}$.

In the second quadrant $\tan x<0$, so $\tan x=-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{21}}$. Answer D.
The integral is the area of a quarter circle of radius 8: $\displaystyle\int_0^8\sqrt{64-x^2}\,dx=\dfrac{\pi\times 8^2}{4}=16\pi$. Answer D.
At $A$ the gradient is negative and the graph is concave up, so $f'(x)<0$ and $f''(x)>0$. Answer B.

$x^2+10x+y^2=11$

$x^2+10x+25+y^2=11+25$

$(x+5)^2+y^2=36$

Circle centre $(-5,0)$, radius $6$. Domain $-11\le x\le 1$ and range $-6\le y\le 6$. Answer C.
Displacement is a maximum when $v$ changes from $v>0$ to $v<0$, that is at $t=10$. Answer B.

Amplitude: $\dfrac12\Rightarrow 1$, so doubled.

Period: $\dfrac{2\pi}{6}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\Rightarrow\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, so doubled. Answer D.

$y=\cos\left(2\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)$ has period $\dfrac{2\pi}{2}=\pi$ and is translated $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ to the right.

So it crosses at $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}+\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{11\pi}{12}$. Answer C.
$f(x)=e^{|x|}+3$ is symmetric about the $y$-axis, so it is an even function. Answer A.

solutions.question: 11(f)
solutions.latex:
$$\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big(\ln(\sin x)-\ln(1+\cos x)\Big)=\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}-\dfrac{-\sin x}{1+\cos x}$$
$$=\dfrac{\cos x(1+\cos x)+\sin^2x}{\sin x(1+\cos x)}=\dfrac{\cos x+\cos^2x+\sin^2x}{\sin x(1+\cos x)}=\dfrac{1+\cos x}{\sin x(1+\cos x)}=\dfrac{1}{\sin x}=\text{cosec}\,x$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: correct answer; 1: use of log laws; 1: correct derivatives of both terms; 1: common denominator and use of $\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$; 1: simplification to $\text{cosec}\,x$

solutions.question: 11(g)
solutions.latex:
$x=\dfrac{h}{\tan10^\circ}$ and $x^2+y^2=940^2$ (triangle $SEF$ is right angled at the base of the tower).

$$\left(\dfrac{h}{\tan8^\circ}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{h}{\tan10^\circ}\right)^2=940^2$$
$$h^2(\cot^28^\circ+\cot^210^\circ)=940^2$$
$$h=\sqrt{\dfrac{940^2}{\cot^28^\circ+\cot^210^\circ}}=103.3\text{ m}$$

The height is 103 metres (to the nearest metre).
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct answer; 1: substitution into $x^2+y^2=940^2$; 1: correct expression for $h$; 1: correct height to nearest metre

solutions.question: 16(a)
solutions.latex:
Geometric part $S_n=2^n$ with $a=2$, $r=2$: $S_{20}=\dfrac{2\left(2^{20}-1\right)}{2-1}=2\,097\,150$ songs.

Arithmetic part $S_n=3n$ with $a=3$, $d=3$: $S_{20}=\dfrac{20}{2}\big(2\times3+(20-1)\times3\big)=630$ songs.

Total songs $=2\,097\,150+630=2\,097\,780$ songs.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct total; 1: geometric sum 2 097 150; 1: arithmetic sum 630; 1: total

solutions.question: 16(b)
solutions.latex:
$A=3x(9-x)^{\frac12}$

$$\dfrac{dA}{dx}=3x\cdot\dfrac12(9-x)^{-\frac12}\cdot(-1)+(9-x)^{\frac12}\cdot3=\dfrac{-3x+6(9-x)}{2\sqrt{9-x}}=\dfrac{54-9x}{2\sqrt{9-x}}$$

Maximum occurs when $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0$: $\dfrac{54-9x}{2\sqrt{9-x}}=0$, so $x=6$ m.

Check using a table:

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} x & 5 & 6 & 7\\ \hline \dfrac{dA}{dx}=\dfrac{54-9x}{2\sqrt{9-x}} & \dfrac{9}{2\sqrt4} & 0 & \dfrac{-9}{2\sqrt2}\\ \hline \text{sign} & + & 0 & - \end{array}$$

Therefore the maximum is when $x=6$ metres.

Alternative method: $\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}=\dfrac{-9(12-x)}{4(9-x)^{\frac32}}$; at $x=6$ this is $-2.598\ldots<0$, so there is a maximum at $x=6$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: correct value of $x$ with justification; 1: derivative by product rule; 1: simplified derivative; 1: $x=6$; 1: test showing maximum

solutions.question: 16(c)
solutions.latex:
$\dfrac{dV}{dt}=R=-k$

$V=-kt+c$

When $t=0$, $V=64$, so $c=64$ and $V=64-kt$.

When $t=9$, $V=1$: $1=64-9k$, $9k=63$, $k=7$.

So $V=64-7t$.

Alternatively: the difference in volume is $63\text{ m}^3$ over 9 hours and the rate of change is constant, so $k=\dfrac{64-1}{9-0}=7$ and $V=64-7t$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: complete working; 1: initial volume 64 and $V=64-kt$; 1: use of $t=9$, $V=1$; 1: $k=7$

solutions.question: 16(c)
solutions.latex:
If the cube has edge length 2 m, the volume will be $8\text{ m}^3$.

$8=64-7t$, $7t=56$, $t=8$.

The cube will have edge length 2 m after 8 hours.

notes: Abbotsleigh 2021 HSC Course Assessment Task 4 (AT4), bundled worked solutions on pages 42-55 (0-based). Section I 10 marks (Q1-10), Section II 90 marks (Q11-16, 15 each). Section II questions that group unrelated items were split per spec into 11(a)..11(g), 12(a)..12(g), 13(a)..13(c), 14(a)..14(d), 15(a)..15(c), 16(a)..16(c) (37 questions in all); the paper's own sub-part labels (i), (ii) were shifted up to (a), (b) and kept in src_label; the cross reference 'answer in (i)' in 13(c) was changed to '(a)'. Typos in the paper left as printed: Q2 'What is the value tan x of given that' (should read 'What is the value of tan x given that'); 12(c)(ii) 'find the probability. that they like soccer only'; 12(f) 'three transformation'; 13(a)(iii) 'least-squared'; 13(c)(i) 'current to the nearest centimetre' (should be 'correct'); 13(c) 'distance travelled by the particle' but the stem says ball; 14(b) 'correct 1 decimal place' (should be '...to 1 decimal place'). Typos in the solutions: 11(g) solutions label parts '(g)(i)' and '(h)(ii)'; 16(a)(ii) solution writes '20 971 150' in the total line instead of 2 097 150 (final total 2 097 780 is right); 15(c)(iii) solution writes e^{0..3219t}. Solution to 11(g)(ii) mentions triangle 'SEF' - I wrote it as the right-angled triangle formed by the two surveyors and the tower base (the solution only says 'triangle is right angled'). Flags: 11(g) set old_syllabus (3D trigonometry); 13(a) set standard_topic (bivariate data). Possibly also Standard-course content (not flagged, for a human to decide): 11(d) Pareto chart, 12(a) cumulative frequency/ogive and median, 12(e) mean of a data set.
